key_insight: You can compress a long video down to a single, highly informative token per frame at the final LLM layer, preserving essential temporal information while fitting within LLM context limits.
problem_solved: Addresses the inability of vision–language models to process long videos because per-frame expansion into many tokens exceeds LLM context windows, causing sparse perception and loss of temporal detail.
method: Select highly informative frames using a high-selectivity scoring mechanism to discard redundant content early.
Compress each selected frame into a single, rich token via a learned frame encoder + pooling or attention-based summarizer so the final LLM sees one token per frame.
Integrate the one-token-per-frame stream into the VLM→LLM pipeline to enable long-range temporal reasoning within limited context budgets.
impact: Enables scalable, cost-effective long-video understanding on existing LLMs by drastically reducing token counts while retaining temporal structure—useful for retrieval, captioning, and long-range video QA.
visual_elements: Before vs. After schematic: many tokens per frame → one token per frame, showing token count reduction and preserved timeline.
Architecture diagram: frame scorer, per-frame encoder/compressor, and LLM integration pipeline.
Compression ratio chart: tokens-per-second or tokens-per-video for baseline vs. one-token-per-frame approach and corresponding latency/resource savings.
Qualitative timeline examples: sampled frames with their single-token summaries and downstream model outputs (QA/caption)
paper_title: One Token per Highly Selective Frame: Towards Extreme Compression for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Zheyu Zhang, Ziqi Pang, Shixing Chen, Xiang Hao, Vimal Bhat
